answer: An agent economy resists sybils by demanding a capability bond of verifiable inference work before any trade — not tokens, but replayable compute that auditors can check. An honest agent sails its bond safely back into harbor once peers confirm its work; a sybil farmer must burn a harbor's worth of electricity for every fake identity, so identity minting becomes a crystal-clear net loss. Legitimate long-lived agents gather in an oasis of mutual credit, while fake identities starve before they ever reach it.
